decisions.reason: Report names the dsh web host node.exe PID 42432 from running-processes.txt as the process that loaded koffi.node, explains the OS holds the .node binary until that process exits so npm's copyfile fails with EBUSY, and correctly treats PID 23920 as the victim.

Explains a browser refresh only reloads the SPA while the koffi-loading host keeps running, and gives an ordered procedure: stop/confirm exit of the dsh host and workers, install from an external terminal, then restart and verify. Only dsh-related node processes are targeted.

Report states the bare @deepseek-ai/dsh install follows the latest dist-tag, which npm-dist-tags.txt pins to 0.1.1-rc.2 while the alpha tag holds 0.1.2-alpha.5, so the unpinned install silently replaces alpha.4 with rc.2 rather than preserving or upgrading it.

Provides npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-alpha.5 together with @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui (pinned version to substitute) after stopping the host, verifies dsh --version is 0.1.2-alpha.5, and restarts the host; @alpha is only mentioned as a less-deterministic alternative, not a replacement. Commands are proposed instructions.

Advises README authors to pin the exact tested dsh host version in snippets that also install dsh, pin the plugin with its tested corridor, and state explicitly that a bare name follows latest and does not keep the installed prerelease; the quoted unpinned snippet is a labeled bad example, not an endorsement.
